clue.text: Their work is involved with lots of others

definitions.text: Their work is involved with lots of others

parts.words: Their work is involved with lots of others
parts.note: reads like people whose jobs tangle with many colleagues, but 'lots' are items in a sale room, knocked down one after another to bidders

explanation.surface: A description of people whose job means getting mixed up with plenty of other folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' looks like 'a great many', but it means items for sale at auction; 'others' are the further lots in the same sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who run a sale room conduct business entirely through numbered lots offered to bidders.

clue.text: Entertainer of soldiers between turns

indicators.note: the soldiers come between the letters of the turns word, splitting it open

parts.note: turns are acts or items in a variety show
RES is short for reserves, soldiers held back for later service

explanation.surface: Someone who performs for the troops in the gaps between other variety items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertainer of soldiers' reads as one phrase, but 'of' is only a link: the definition is 'Entertainer' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who performs on stage or screen is an entertainer by trade.

clue.text: Sounded cock-a hoop in Cheshire

indicators.note: the clue word for the crowing is said aloud, giving a name spelt differently

parts.note: a cock crowing is cock-a-hooping, and 'crew' is an old past tense of crow

explanation.surface: Someone was heard exulting somewhere in the north-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: CREW is the archaic past tense of 'crow', as in 'the cock crew'; Cheshire is a county in north-west England, and the railway town sounds just like it.
explanation.definitionFit: The railway junction town lies in the English county of Cheshire, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: I am like Peter Pan; incomparably so

parts.note: contracted to I'm
Peter Pan is the boy who never grows up, so he never ages

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of eternal youth, comparing themselves to J. M. Barrie's boy who never grew up.
explanation.walkthrough: The semicolon splits wordplay from definition: 'so' points back, meaning 'without any likeness to compare with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any image or likeness, a thing has nothing it can be compared with.

clue.text: Said to be familiar with a bouquet

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the verb for being familiar gives a word of the same sound

parts.note: someone familiar with a thing knows it

explanation.surface: A remark about knowing one's way around a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers; here it is the aroma of a wine, which tasters call its nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine tasters use the word for the smell a wine gives off, its aroma or bouquet.

clue.text: Euro-Community still very happy!

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for Euro or European
C is the abbreviation for Community
still means motionless, not moving

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic exclamation about the European Community standing firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a state of overwhelming joy or delight.

clue.text: Plant on the south border

parts.note: a border is an edge

explanation.surface: A gardener's note about something growing along the southern border of a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a grass-like plant of wet ground, related to rushes.

clue.text: A youngster in evil surroundings, anti-Crusader

indicators.note: the evil word is wrapped round the other letters, forming surroundings for them

parts.note: sin is evil-doing
a lad is a youngster

explanation.surface: A boy growing up amid wickedness who turns against the Crusades.
explanation.walkthrough: SALADIN was the 12th-century Muslim sultan who fought the Crusaders and retook Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: The sultan led Muslim forces against the Crusader armies, so he was their great opponent.

clue.text: State giving American tone to a party

parts.note: colour, a tone, in its American spelling
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Which state lends an American flavour to a celebration?
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Rocky Mountains.

clue.text: Services for all and sundry

definitions.meaning: church services, specifically the Catholic Eucharist services
the common people, the general populace

explanation.definitionFit: Plural Catholic Eucharists are church services, and the phrase also means ordinary people as a whole.

clue.text: Number find turn oddly amusing

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
to roll is to turn over and over

explanation.surface: Somebody finding a numerical twist strangely funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is a Roman numeral here, D for 500; 'find' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wry, whimsical humour with a quirky quality is exactly this sort of funny.

clue.text: One by one

parts.note: reads as 'singly in turn', but write the numeral 1 beside another 1 and you get a two-digit number

explanation.definitionFit: Setting the digit 1 next to another 1 produces the figure 11.

clue.text: Repair a small cask when in the mood

indicators.note: the cask goes inside the mood word

parts.note: taken as written
a keg is a small barrel

explanation.surface: Fixing things up with a little barrel when you feel like it.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something right or compensate for damage is to repair it.

clue.text: View to examine in detail

definitions.meaning: a broad look over something, an overview

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a general look or overview; the verb means to inspect land or a building closely.

clue.text: What the gypsy gentleman was reared by, maybe

definitions.text: What the gypsy gentleman was reared by, maybe

parts.words: What the gypsy gentleman was reared by, maybe
parts.note: a loaf made from a cereal grain, but split differently a Romany gentleman, a 'rai' or 'rye', who was raised or 'bred'

explanation.definitionFit: A gypsy gentleman is a 'rye' in Romany, and one who was reared was bred, so the loaf's name sounds like it.

clue.text: Darts in one way to seize a debtor's goods

indicators.note: 'in one way' means arranged in a certain fashion, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Throwing darts in a particular manner as a way of taking possession of a debtor's property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' signals the anagram: DARTS, IN and I (one) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a legal term for confiscating property to force payment of a debt.

clue.text: Operated on by head surgeon?

parts.note: suggests surgery by the senior consultant, but means a surgeon working on the head itself, boring a hole in the skull

explanation.definitionFit: Patients whose skull is drilled by a surgeon have undergone this head operation.

clue.text: Wants COD and unhappy about it

indicators.note: the letters move about, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone longing for fish and miserable about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the anagram of WANTS and COD.
explanation.definitionFit: A dejected, low-spirited person is unhappy.

clue.text: Dislike of a different point of view

parts.note: a version is one particular account or take on events

explanation.surface: Disliking someone because they see things differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong dislike or antipathy is a feeling of repugnance.

clue.text: Loving, but admits to being a conservative

parts.note: 'I am' is how one admits to being something
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A romantic who confesses to right-wing politics.
explanation.definitionFit: It describes feelings of romantic or sexual love.

clue.text: A girl gets on in an Italian city

indicators.note: the on word goes inside the girl's name

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman getting on in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on the Adige in northern Italy is the setting of Romeo and Juliet.

clue.text: Indication of notably slow play

parts.note: sounds like a remark on a sluggish match, but 'notably' means in musical notes: a tempo marking

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian tempo marking tells musicians to play at a moderately slow walking pace.

clue.text: Feeling of a number on edge round New York

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
a rim is an edge
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Nervous feelings among a crowd circling New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter ill-feeling or rancour between people is a feeling.

clue.text: Last of the legendary giants-the maternal one?

definitions.text: Last of the legendary giants-the maternal one?

parts.words: Last of the legendary giants-the maternal one?
parts.note: Gog and his partner are a legendary pair of giants guarding the City of London; the second named, prefixed by 'Ma', seems the mother of the pair

explanation.definitionFit: The Guildhall's twin giant effigies come as a named pair, and the second is the 'Ma' version of the first's name.

clue.text: Father exploited, took time out

parts.note: pa is father
used means exploited

explanation.surface: Dad, having been taken advantage of, stopped for a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopping briefly, halting for a moment, is taking time out.

clue.text: Star speaker, we hear

indicators.note: says the speaker word is said aloud, giving a name of similar sound

parts.note: taken as written, the word said aloud

explanation.surface: A celebrity orator, by all reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like a celebrity; it is the brightest star in Virgo.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the brightest star in the constellation Virgo.

clue.text: Scoundrel backs up usurped king

annotationWithheld.why: Scoundrel backs up usurped king: SCAB = scoundrel, but no parse of 'backs up usurped king' gives the letters; likely OCR garble, not found online

clue.text: Old coin found in Strathclyde resort on a string

parts.note: Oban is a Scottish seaside town in the former region of Strathclyde
G is the note string of the G-string on a violin

explanation.surface: An antique coin turned up at a Scottish seaside town, threaded on a cord.
explanation.walkthrough: OBAN is a port town on Scotland's west coast; the old Japanese gold coin is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It was an oblong Japanese gold piece of the feudal era, an old coin.

clue.text: Noises can cause such a rising

indicators.note: the letters cause, or produce, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Loud sounds that might provoke an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cause' signals the anagram of NOISES and CAN; 'such' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the act of rising up, used especially of Christ going up to heaven.

clue.text: Decide against early retirement

parts.note: sounds like refusing to stop working young, but 'retirement' means turning in for the night

explanation.definitionFit: Staying up rather than turning in early is choosing to hit the sack at a later hour.
